title: Moonflowers and efficient code sparsification
summary: We introduce \emph{moonflowers}, a weaker analogue of sunflowers. A family of sets $S_1,\ldots,S_k$ is a $k$-moonflower if each set $S_i$ contains at least one element that is absent from all the others. We study the extremal problem of determining the largest possible size of a family of sets of size at most $w$ that avoids a $k$-moonflower, and obtain near-optimal bounds. As an application, we revisit the code sparsification problem studied by Brakensiek and Guruswami (STOC 2025) and improve the bounds to near optimal.
